subject: Learning Methods
title: Motivated Forgetting
description: A quick win: understand Motivated Forgetting.

hook.text: Freud believed people push painful memories out of consciousness. He called it repression.

buildup.text: Modern research confirms a version of this: people can deliberately suppress unwanted memories.

discovery.text: The think/no-think paradigm shows that suppressing retrieval weakens the memory over repeated attempts.

twist.text: Suppression is an active process. The prefrontal cortex literally inhibits hippocampal activity during it.

climax.text: This has implications for trauma. Avoidance may actually weaken traumatic memories, for better or worse.

punchline.text: The brain can choose to forget. It takes real effort.

quiz.question: What does the think/no-think paradigm demonstrate?
options: People cannot control what they remember
Deliberately suppressing retrieval weakens the memory
